body_markdown:
AI summary


Ekho's documentation is rebuilt around four sections. The buyer and Sales Agent guides are open in full, the Transaction Engine opens on a short preview, and the API reference appears once an Ekho client signs in. It is AI-powered: generated from the reality of our codebase so it updates itself, and you can ask it a question in your own words at docs.ekho.com.


Ekho's documentation has been rebuilt. It is now four sections instead of one undifferentiated pile: a guide for buyers, a guide for the AI Sales Agent, a guide for the Transaction Engine, and a full API reference.


##


A section for each reader


Buyers get the plain-language path: finding a vehicle, building an order, paying, protecting it, titling and registering, and taking delivery. Dealers get a guide per product. Developers get the API reference, with the SDK, webhooks and error types beside it.


##


Open to anyone


The buyer guide and the AI Sales Agent guide are public in full. No account, no sign-in, nothing to request. If you are weighing up the Sales Agent, you can read how it is set up, what it does on each channel and how it handles a lead, before you speak to anyone here.


##


Before you sign in


The Transaction Engine opens on a short preview: what the product is, how it works, and what a buyer sees. That is enough to judge whether it fits. The operating guide underneath it, covering your orders, financing, titling and payouts, is for Ekho clients, and so is the API reference, which appears once you sign in.


##


Always current, and you can just ask it


The documentation is AI-powered. It is generated from the reality of our codebase and updates itself as the product changes, so it does not drift until someone remembers to rewrite it. What you read is what the product actually does today.


You also do not have to hunt through it. At[docs.ekho.com](https://docs.ekho.com/) you can ask a question in your own words and get the answer straight out of the docs.


##


Where to find it


Read it at[docs.ekho.com](https://docs.ekho.com/) . From the Admin Portal, the documentation link carries your session, so you arrive signed in and the client sections are simply there.
